drills.q: Assets: 400 Treasuries (0%), 300 retail (75%), 200 corporate unrated (100%). RWA and density?
drills.a: RWA = 0 + 225 + 200 = 425. Density = 425/900 = 47.2%. Same assets, different mix - composition IS capital strategy.

drills.q: CET1 = 150, used RWA = 1,800. Ratio vs the 7% all-in minimum? Surplus in dollars?
drills.a: Ratio = 150/1800 = 8.33%. Minimum needs 0.07 x 1800 = 126. Surplus = 24mm. Note G-SIBs with SCB face low-teens effective requirements - check which requirement applies before celebrating.

drills.q: IRB RWA = 1,000; standardized RWA = 1,600. Full-phase floor: which RWA is used?
drills.a: Floor = 0.725 x 1600 = 1160 > 1000 -> floor binds, use 1160. The internal models' 20% advantage shrinks to nothing beyond the floor; at mid phase-in (e.g., 65%) floor = 1040, still binding.

drills.q: HQLA: Level1 = 300, Level2A = 150. Compute capped HQLA.
drills.a: L2A cap = 40% of total HQLA: solve L2A <= 0.4(300+L2A) -> L2A <= 200. 150 < 200 so uncapped: HQLA = 450. If net outflows were 400, LCR = 112.5% - pass.

drills.q: Why can a bank pass LCR/NSFR and still fail in days? Give the 2023 example mechanics.
drills.a: Metrics assume runoff rates over 30 days/1 year calibrated to history. SVB: ~90% uninsured deposits ran within ~48 hours via mobile banking after a Twitter-era panic - far faster than any assumption - while HTM unrealized losses (~$15B+) meant selling HQLA created capital holes. Speed + rate risk broke calibration.

drills.q: Your desk's IMM capital beats SA by 40%. Bank-wide benefit under full output floor?
drills.a: Bank-wide modeled RWA still cannot drop below 72.5% of SA total, so the whole-bank benefit caps at 27.5% regardless of desk-level wins. Desk optimization matters only where aggregate modeled RWA sits above the floor.

drills.q: Name two reasons Basel II's IRB amplified procyclicality.
drills.a: 1) Through-the-cycle PD/LGD estimates updated downward in booms expanded credit exactly when risks built; 2) downturn LGDs/PDs realized point-in-time in busts forced capital raises at market bottoms (fire-sale dynamics). Basel IV's floors + revised SA reduce model-driven amplitude.

drills.q: What did the RCAP/RWA dispersion studies show and what reform did they trigger?
drills.a: Near-identical portfolios carried roughly 2x different RWA across banks depending on internal-model choices - undermining comparability and trust. Triggered Basel IV: revised SA as benchmark, IRB input floors, and the 72.5% output floor capping model variance.

drills.q: A quarter-end RWA figure doesn't reconcile against finance's general ledger, requiring manual adjustment entries. What's the likely root cause and fix?
drills.a: Likely cause: the risk-data-aggregation pipeline uses a different position snapshot time, netting logic, or currency-conversion path than the general ledger -- a classic BCBS 239 gap. Fix: establish a single golden-source data lineage feeding both finance and risk pipelines identically, with automated daily (not quarter-end-only) reconciliation controls.

drills.q: Design question: you're the Principal engineer for a regional bank that just crossed $100B in assets and picked up LCR/NSFR obligations for the first time. What's your first-quarter plan, and how do you handle a board deadline that arrives before the proper build is done?
drills.a: Start with data lineage and product-taxonomy mapping (classifying every deposit/loan/security into regulatory categories), not the ratio arithmetic -- that classification work is the real bottleneck. Build the mapping layer as versioned, testable, auditable code decoupled from the aggregation math. Stand up automated daily reconciliation against treasury/finance cash-flow systems immediately. If the board wants numbers in six weeks, deliver a clearly-labeled interim manual/semi-automated calculation with documented conservative assumptions and explicit gaps, continuing the proper automated build in parallel -- a precise-looking number on unreconciled data is worse than a clearly-caveated interim estimate.
